study_identification_part.si4_title: A neuroimaging measure to capture heterogeneous patterns of atrophy in Parkinson's disease and dementia with Lewy bodies

cm1_research_objectives.reason: The study objectives are clearly stated in both the abstract and the introduction. The researchers aim to quantify patterns of neurodegenerative dissimilarity in Parkinson's disease (PD) and Dementia with Lewy bodies (DLB) using neuroanatomical normative modeling and evaluate the clinical relevance of the 'total outlier count' by testing its association with cognitive and disease-specific measures. Specific hypotheses are also provided.
cm1_research_objectives.supporting_text: We aimed to quantify patterns of neurodegenerative dissimilarity in participants with PD and DLB and evaluate the potential clinical relevance of total outlier count by testing its association with key clinical measures in PD and DLB. ... We hypothesised that there would be a) significant differences in total number of regional outliers between high and poor visual performance PD groups, and in PD compared with DLB; b) greater dissimilarity in individual patients for low versus high visual performers in PD; and for DLB compared to PD. Finally, we predicted c) that greater total outlier count would be associated with poorer cognitive performance in PD and DLB.

nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.reason: This study uses an existing normative model (Rutherford et al., 2022) which is cited. For the local recalibration, eligibility criteria for the reference sample (controls) are described for both the UCL site and the NACC dataset. Image quality standards (visual inspection) are specified, and final sample sizes for the controls are reported.
nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.supporting_text: Rutherford and colleagues (Rutherford et al., 2022) modelled normative lifespan curves for cortical thicknesses across 148 regions ... Their reference cohort comprised 58,836 participants from 82 sites. ... Controls were recruited from spouses of patients and UCL volunteer databases. Inclusion criteria were being aged 50–80 and exclusions were the presence of past neurological or psychiatric history, or cognitive impairment on history or neuropsychological testing. ... Controls in the NACC dataset had no evidence of cognitive impairment or history of neurological illness. ... Processed images were quality controlled by visually inspecting grey and white matter boundaries, and subcortical segmentation boundaries ... we included ... 165 controls (38 from UCL, 127 from NACC), used to calibrate the reference dataset models to the study data

nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.reason: The study describes that the existing normative model used age and sex as covariates and accounted for site differences. For the current study, recalibration was performed using an adapted transfer learning approach to account for site and scanner differences.
nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.supporting_text: modelled normative lifespan curves for cortical thicknesses ... using a warped Bayesian Linear Regression with age and sex as covariates, and accounting for site differences (Bayer et al., 2022). ... The reference normative model was recalibrated to the study datasets with an adapted transfer learning approach (Kia et al., 2022). This involved inputting control data from our two study sites into the reference normative model to generate stable parameters ... to account for residual differences in data distributions, caused by factors such as scanner differences.

nm4_image_acquisition_protocol.reason: For the primary data collection at the UCL site (which includes controls used for recalibration), the imaging modality, equipment (3T Siemens Magnetom Prisma), and specific acquisition parameters (TR, TE, resolution, etc.) are provided. For the secondary NACC data, the equipment is mentioned and further details are referenced to the database.
nm4_image_acquisition_protocol.supporting_text: Structural T1w-MRI scans at UCL were acquired on a 3 T Siemens Magnetom Prisma scanner with a 64-channel head coil. Structural magnetisation prepared rapid acquisition gradient echo (MPRAGE) data were acquired using the following parameters: 1 × 1 × 1 mm voxel, TE = 3.34 ms, TR = 2530 ms, flip angle = 7°, acquisition time = 9 min. Structural T1w-MRI scans from NACC ADRC '8361' were acquired on 1.5 T GE scanners (further information on scanning parameters are available via the NACC database).

nm5_data_preprocessing.reason: The preprocessing software (FreeSurfer v6.0.0) and the specific pipeline ('recon-all') are specified. Quality control procedures (visual inspection by a blinded researcher) are also described.
nm5_data_preprocessing.supporting_text: The 'recon-all' function in FreeSurfer v6.0.0 (http://www.freesurfer.net) was used to process all UCL and NACC MRI data. ... Processed images were quality controlled by visually inspecting grey and white matter boundaries, and subcortical segmentation boundaries superimposed on the corresponding structural T1-weighted image by a researcher blind to clinical status.

cr1_selection_criteria_clinical_cohort.supporting_text: They were diagnosed as having PD or probable DLB if they satisfied Queen Square Brain Bank PD diagnostic criteria (Daniel and Lees, 1993) and the Dementia with Lewy Bodies Consortium Criteria (McKeith et al., 2017) respectively. Exclusions were a history of traumatic brain injury, or major co-morbid psychiatric or confounding neurological disorders ... Presence of dementia was also an exclusion criterion [for PD] ... Participants from site '8361' [NACC] were included if they had ... 1) dementia diagnosis; 2) primary or contributing cause of cognitive impairment: Lewy body disease; 3) not classed as MCI; and 4) absence of a diagnosis of PD. ... cr2_handling_of_clinical_covariates.supporting_text: Linear regressions, correcting for age and sex, were used to test for group differences in total outlier count ... In exploratory analyses, we tested associations with disease-specific measures including ... (MDS-UPDRS), motor severity (MDS-UPDRS-III), hallucination severity (UM-PDHQ) and depression score (HADS).

cr6_interpretation_of_deviation_scores.reason: The meaning and threshold for deviation scores (z-scores < -1.96) are explained as representing regional outliers/atrophy. The direction of the scores is interpreted, and clinical implications are discussed in relation to cognitive performance.
cr6_interpretation_of_deviation_scores.supporting_text: outliers were defined as z-scores < -1.96. This is a commonly used threshold representing 95 % confidence that points below it differ from the mean ... and since we are interested in atrophy, only consider lower values ... The total number of outliers ... was summed per participant to provide the total outlier count. ... Neuroanatomical normative modelling shows promise as a clinically informative technique in PD and DLB ... total outlier count was significantly associated with severity of cognitive measures in both DLB and PD.
